{{Short description|American mathematician}}
'''Ronald John Stern''' (born 20 January 1947) is a mathematician who works on [[topology]], [[geometry]], and [[gauge theory]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://faculty.sites.uci.edu/rstern/ |title=Ronald J. Stern |publisher=Faculty.sites.uci.edu |date= |access-date=2015-06-18}}</ref> He is emeritus professor at the [[University of California, Irvine]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.faculty.uci.edu/profile.cfm?faculty_id=2168 |title=UC Irvine - Faculty Profile System |publisher=Faculty.uci.edu |date=2007-05-14 |access-date=2015-06-18}}</ref>

Stern was the first in his family to receive a college education and earned his bachelor's degree in mathematics from [[Knox College (Illinois)|Knox College]] in [[Galesburg, Illinois]].<ref name="deanannounce">{{cite news|last1=Addison|first1=Lisa|last2=Canalis|first2=John|title=UCI Names Dean of Physical Sciences|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1998-jun-13-me-59543-story.html|access-date=9 August 2017|work=Los Angeles Times|date=13 June 1998}}</ref> He then earned his Ph.D. in 1973 from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] under the joint supervision of [[Robert Duncan Edwards]] <small>([[:de:Robert Duncan Edwards|de]])</small> and Robert F. Brown.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://genealogy.math.uni-bielefeld.de/id.php?id=12408 |title=The Mathematics Genealogy Project - Ronald Stern |publisher=Genealogy.math.uni-bielefeld.de |date= |access-date=2015-06-18}}</ref>

Before joining the faculty at the University of California, Irvine in 1989, Stern was a professor at the [[University of Utah]] and a visiting professor at UCLA and the [[University of Hawaii]].<ref name="deanannounce"/>

He was an Invited Speaker at the 1998 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], in [[Berlin]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=Stern |title=International Mathematical Union (IMU) |publisher=Mathunion.org |date= |access-date=2015-06-18}}</ref>

He is a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list-institution |title=Fellows of the AMS by Institution |publisher=Ams.org |date=2015-04-13 |access-date=2015-06-18}}</ref>

==Selected papers==
These are his most cited papers (according to [[Google Scholar]]), they are all joint work with [[Ron Fintushel]]:<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=HUEZguIAAAAJ |title=Ronald J. Stern - Google Scholar Citations |date= |access-date=2015-06-18}}</ref>
*"Knots, links, and 4-manifolds", ''[[Inventiones mathematicae]]'' 134 (2), pp.&nbsp;363–400 (1998)
*"Rational blowdowns of smooth 4-manifolds", ''[[Journal of Differential Geometry]]'' 46 (2), pp.&nbsp;181–235 (1997)
*"Instanton homology of Seifert fibred homology three spheres", ''[[Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society]]'' 61 (3), pp.&nbsp;109–137 (1990)
*"Immersed spheres in 4-manifolds and the immersed Thom conjecture", ''[[Turkish Journal of Mathematics]]'' 19 (2), pp.&nbsp;145–157 (1995)
*"Pseudofree orbifolds", ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]'', pp.&nbsp;335–364 (1985)
*"Constructing lens spaces by surgery on knots", ''[[Mathematische Zeitschrift]]'' 175 (1), pp.&nbsp;33–51 (1980)
*"The blowup formula for Donaldson invariants", ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]'' 143 (3), pp.&nbsp;529–546 (1996)
